subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue the Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split as a core architecture track, and what is the first supported milestone?
rationale: The remaining work requires choosing public protocol, config, security, lifecycle, deployment, and migration boundaries; automation cannot safely pick those product and security contracts.

options.title: Approve phased runtime split
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines the local-split protocol, trust model, lifecycle semantics, and session/delivery migration before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow to execution placement
options.body: Treat #82017 and #84758 as the current implementation scope while leaving the broader Gateway split deferred until placement and worker-security contracts settle.

options.title: Defer core architecture change
options.body: Keep improving multi-gateway, plugin, harness, and lifecycle workarounds without committing to a distributed runtime boundary yet.

recommendation.title: Approve phased runtime split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines the local-split protocol, trust model, lifecycle semantics, and session/delivery migration before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest combined signal from current Gateway/agent runtime history and the open worker-runtime isolation experiment linked to the RFC.
